claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children would you like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex, who's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! You're very welcome – I'm happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Now, could you tell me: **Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

Next question: **Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep (for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Lovely, thank you. That's helpful to know.

Just a couple more questions to make sure everything is in order:

**Is Alex currently in any of the following situations?**
- In hospital for an extended period
- In local authority care
- In residential accommodation paid for by the local council

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he was in local authority care for a short while recently, but it was just for a couple of months.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. That's helpful information.

Could you clarify a bit more about Alex's care situation:

**Has Alex now returned home to live with you, and if so, how long ago did he come back?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's back home with me now. He's been home for a little while - it was just a temporary situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. It's good to know Alex is back home with you now.

Just to confirm the timeline: **Was Alex in local authority care for more than 8 weeks in total?** And while he was in care, **did the local council pay towards his accommodation or maintenance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, it wasn't more than 8 weeks - it was 7 weeks total. And yes, the local council did pay for his accommodation while he was there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for those details – that's very helpful.

Since Alex was in local authority care for 7 weeks (which is under the 8-week threshold) and he's now back home living with you, this shouldn't affect your eligibility.

Just one more question to make sure: **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Based on everything you've told me, I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

- ✅ **You live in the UK**
- ✅ **Alex is under 16 years old** (he's 6)
- ✅ **You are responsible for Alex** – he lives with you at home
- ✅ **Alex's time in local authority care was under 8 weeks** (7 weeks), so this doesn't affect your eligibility
- ✅ **No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex**

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. If you haven't already, you'll need to apply through the official government channels.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
